narrative.overview:
Vero.io is built for commercial operators who move fast and need the full picture at a glance. The interface does not explain itself; it performs. Every screen is a live readout: data that moves, statuses that update, pipeline that runs. The visual language comes from command-and-control environments — deep-void backgrounds that make colored signals impossible to miss, a single violet accent that marks every actionable moment, and a typographic system that sorts information by urgency rather than by aesthetics.

The system is dark because the work happens in sessions, not glances. An SDR opening the Contact Manager at 9am expects a surface that reduces eye strain across a full workday, not a light canvas that shouts. The darkness is purposeful: it makes pipeline-green and signal-purple land with precision.

This system explicitly rejects generic SaaS neutrality — Notion-cream backgrounds, Linear-style minimalism indistinguishable from 200 other B2B tools, and the overdesigned startup aesthetic (neon glow, decorative glassmorphism, gradient text everywhere).
keyCharacteristics: Deep-void dark theme: #0B0E14 base, tonal surface layers rising to #141920
Signal Purple (#8A5CF5) as the single accent: active states, primary CTAs, the brand mark itself
Status colors carry semantic weight: pipeline-green for valid/enriched, amber for threshold warnings, red for critical
Inter at extreme weights (800 extrabold for headings, 400 for body, 600 for labels)
Monospace data values: numbers and codes always ui-monospace — they are data, not prose
Glow shadows on accent elements only; surfaces are flat at rest
Label text in uppercase with wide tracking (0.15em) as the wayfinding layer

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Signal Purple (#8A5CF5) appears on at most one primary action per screen. If everything is purple, nothing signals.

rules.name: The Semantic Triad Rule
rules.body: Green means valid or enriched. Amber means threshold or pending. Red means critical or failed. Never use them for visual interest alone.

rules.name: The Weight-or-Size Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy is expressed through either weight or size — not both simultaneously and not color alone.

rules.name: The Mono Data Rule
rules.body: Any value that is a count, identifier, percentage, or timestamp is monospace. Inline numbers in prose are the one exception.

rules.name: The Flat-at-Rest Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat. Glow appears only in response to interaction state or semantic emphasis. A card that glows at rest has lost its signal value.

dos: Do use Signal Purple (#8A5CF5) for one primary action per screen
Do use monospace (ui-monospace) for all numeric data: credit counts, enrichment percentages, contact IDs, timestamps
Do express hierarchy through weight or size contrast of at least 1.25x between levels
Do tint hover states with Signal Purple at low opacity (5–20%) for interactive elements
Do use uppercase labels with 0.15em letter-spacing for category and section identifiers
Do keep the dark theme's surface stack strict: #0B0E14 → #0F1318 → #141920
Do use glow shadows on primary CTAs and live indicators only
donts: Don't make the interface look like a generic SaaS tool: no Notion-cream backgrounds, no Linear-style blank minimalism
Don't use overdesigned decoration: glassmorphism as default styling, neon-on-black aesthetics
Don't use gradient text (background-clip: text) in new components — use solid Signal Purple Light (#A78BFA) for emphasis instead
Don't render identical cards in a uniform grid without variation in size, weight, or structure
Don't apply glow shadows to surfaces at rest
Don't use Signal Purple for more than one primary element per screen
Don't use border-left or border-right as a colored accent stripe on cards, alerts, or list items
Don't drop data labels below Text Subtle (#4A5568) — that is the contrast floor
Don't enterprise-gray this interface with heavy visual weight, excessive table chrome, or the Salesforce aesthetic
